thread.title: Warren Buffett’s charity lunch auction for S.F.’s Glide sells for $3.3 million

author: Mark Calvey
title: Warren Buffett’s charity lunch auction for S.F.’s Glide sells for $3.3 million
text: – Senior Reporter, San Francisco Business Times Jun 1, 2018, 10:14pm PDT The winner of eBay’s annual auction for lunch with Warren Buffett picked up a tab of $3,300,100, which goes to the San Francisco-based Glide Foundation to help the city’s homeless and others in need. The winning bidder wished to remain anonymous, Glide said. Glide President and CEO Karen Hanrahan said that the strong bidding on the Buffett lunch comes at a good time. Glide is seeing rising demand for its services even as San Francisco is said to be enjoying the strongest economy since World War II. "San Francisco is this incredible place, where there trends are going in opposite directions," Hanrahan told the San Francisco Business Times shortly after the auction closed Friday night. "You have this incredible wealth that's growing and so many people are benefitting from it. At the same time, so many indicators of well-being are getting worse, from homelessness and the poverty rate to addiction and the gap between rich and poor." This year's auction got off to a good start with the bidding by mid-week surpassing last year's winning bid of $2,679,001, which was rounded up to $2.7 million by the winner, who also remained anonymous. Still today's winning bid was within striking distance of the record $3,456,789 that was reached in both the 2012 and 2016 auctions. Since the first Buffett charity lunch in 2000, the annual event has raised a total of almost $30 million for Glide. The charity auction gives the winning bidder and seven friends the opportunity to have lunch with Buffett at Smith & Wollensky steakhouse in New York. Glide was founded more than 50 years ago by the husband-and-wife team of Rev. Cecil Williams and Janice Mirikitani . The two joined Glide’s supporters in watching the final moments of bidding at a countdown party in San Francisco's Mid-Market district. Buffett is CEO of Omaha-based Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE: BRK-A) (NYSE: BRK-B), which has extensive holdings in the Bay Area, including an almost 10 percent stake in Wells Fargo (NYSE: WFC) and full ownership of San Francisco-based Business Wire and South San Francisco-based See’s Candies. Berkshire also holds large stakes in several blue-chip companies, including Coca-Cola (NYSE: KO), Bank of America (NYSE: BAC) and Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL). Dubbed "the Oracle of Omaha," Buffett's buy-and-hold investing prowess has gained a large global following and has paid off handsomely; He's the world's third-richest individual with a net worth of $83 billion. Past winners of the mid-Manhattan steakhouse lunch say Buffett orders a medium-rare sirloin steak with hash browns and a Cherry Coke. – Senior Reporter, San Francisco Business Times Jun 1, 2018, 10:14pm PDT Related Content
